newsitem.title: USA: Idaho Power draws down Brownlee reservoir.
newsitem.headline: Idaho Power draws down Brownlee reservoir.

text.p: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers has ordered Idaho Power Co to draw down reservoir storage at its Brownlee Dam on the Snake River in a measure aimed at preventing downstream flooding, the company said.
In a newsletter, Idaho Power said Brownlee would be drawn down to its lowest level in more than 25 years.
A spokesman for the utility said Thursday about half the water being released was spilling rather than running through turbines due to hydraulic capacity limitations and limited demand for power.
In an average water year, the utility's Snake River hydroelectric projects provide about half of Idaho Power's needs, he noted.

"If all of a sudden we have a massive snowmelt...the Corps wants to be sure there is enough empty space in Northwest reservoirs to catch the water and prevent flooding like there was last year in Portland and other downstream cities," said Idaho Power operations analyst Jim James.
Idaho Power began the drawdown on January 24.
The Corps has ordered the water level be reduced 43 feet below maximum capacity at 2,077 feet above sea level to 2,034 feet by the end of February.
By the end of March the level must be reduced another 28 feet to 2,006 feet and by the end of April it will be reduced another 30 feet to 1,976 feet.
"At that point Brownlee will be about two-thirds empty," James said.
He said the utility hopes to begin filling the reservoir as quickly as possible in early May, estimating it will take 7 to 10 days to refill.
